reflection.quote: He who is not contented with what he has, would not be contented with what he would like to have.
reflection.reading:
Sundays used to be the hardest day. Not because anything dramatic happened — the opposite. Sundays were quiet, and quiet was where the noise in my head got loudest. I'd be hungover, or trying not to be, watching the day stretch out with nothing to numb it. The stillness felt like an accusation.

What changed wasn't that Sundays got more exciting. It's that I stopped needing them to be. A slow morning with coffee that I actually taste. A walk without dread. Making something for dinner instead of ordering it because I can't face the door. Texting a friend back the same day. These are the things I couldn't do drunk — not because I was too busy, but because I was too checked out to notice they were available. Sobriety didn't hand me a bigger life first. It handed me a real one, and the bigger life grew out of that.

Socrates was pointing at something the program says in its own way: if you can't be content with what's in front of you today, no future version of your life will fix that. The work isn't chasing a Sunday worth having. It's showing up to this one, sober, and letting it be what it is. That's the whole practice. That's where the rest of it starts.
reflection.meditation: Sit with this Sunday as it actually is. Notice one small thing you couldn't have noticed a year into drinking. Let that be enough for a moment.

affirmations: Today I can be present for a quiet day without needing to escape it.
I am building a life I don't have to check out of.
I have agency over how I meet this day, one hour at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Sunday I can remember. Grateful for the small stuff — coffee that tastes like coffee, a phone I'm not afraid to check, a body that isn't paying for last night. Grateful for the people who stayed and the ones I've met on this side of the decision. And grateful, mostly, for another day where I get to choose again.
gratitude.closing: One more day, one more chance to show up. That's the whole deal.
